title: VRAEM operation kills Shining Path remnant commander 'camarada Richard' one day into Fujimori government
detail: Twenty-four hours after Keiko Fujimori took office, Peruvian armed forces engaged in intense combat with Shining Path (Sendero Luminoso) narco-terrorist remnants at Alto Mantaro in the VRAEM (Valle de los Ríos Apurímac, Ene y Mantaro). The operation killed Jhonny Curo Rojas, alias 'camarada Richard', a senior commander of the group's residual faction, and left one soldier wounded. Air Force helicopters providing tactical support sustained 18 bullet impacts. Security forces recovered weapons, ammunition, explosives, communications equipment and military supplies from the site. President Fujimori visited military bases in the VRAEM to reaffirm her support for the armed forces and police involved.

media.caption: Fujimori expresses support for armed forces after VRAEM antiterrorist operation

title: First Fujimori cabinet meeting agrees to request 120-day emergency legislative powers from Congress
detail: At its first ordinary meeting on July 29, the new Fujimori cabinet agreed to request that Congress delegate legislative powers for 120 days covering security, state reform and the economy. The draft proposal contemplates transferring prison administration and security to the Armed Forces, allowing private administration of some prisons, merging or dissolving state agencies, and a labor-flexibilization package — which Fujimori insisted would not cut existing labor rights. The request must navigate Peru's newly installed bicameral Congress, where left-of-center parties have signaled they will seek to impose conditions before approval, likely pushing a final vote into September.

media.caption: Fujimori's ministers meet to prepare bill requesting legislative powers
